bibl.title: Kilosort: realtime spike-sorting for extracellular electrophysiology with hundreds of channels

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: Here we introduce Kilosort, a spike sorting framework that meets these criteria, and show that it allows rapid and accurate sorting of large-scale in vivo data.

span.label: spike sorting of high-channel-count extracellular recordings
span.quote: When multiple neurons close to the electrode fire action potentials, their spikes must be identified and assigned to the correct neuron based on the features of the recorded waveforms, a process known as spike sorting 1–15.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: Here we overcome these limitations and present Kilosort, a new algorithm which takes advantage of a novel mathematical approach that greatly reduces the amount of calculation required, together with the computing capabilities of low-cost commercially available graphics processing units (GPUs).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Replacing the full matrix convolution by a rank-3 low-rank template decomposition cuts the number of filtering operations by the ratio of channel count to template rank, which is what makes near-realtime sorting of hundreds of channels possible
span.quote: However, the low-rank decomposition of templates allows us to reduce the number of operations by a factor of Nchan/Nrank, where Nchan is the number of channels (typically > 100) and Nrank is the rank of the decomposed template (typically 3).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Over-split clusters arise because the fitting algorithm splits a high-variance cluster across several templates in order to reduce total reconstruction error, which is why the resulting cluster pairs form one continuous density and can be merged automatically
span.quote: Instead, these clusters arise as a consequence of the algorithm partitioning clusters with large variance into multiple templates, so as to better explain their total variance.

span.label: Manual operator curation is still needed despite the automatic merging heuristic, mainly because of electrode drift and other non-stationarities.
span.quote: Although we have defined a heuristic which eliminates the need for many manual merges, operator curation is still required, primarily due to non-stationarities in the recordings such as electrode drift.

span.label: The optimisation can settle in non-optimal local minima, which the authors only ameliorate by annealing several parameters.
span.quote: Like most clustering algorithms, this model is prone to non-optimal local minima.

span.label: The speed comparison against the established framework was not run at the largest channel count, so no 384-channel baseline exists.
span.quote: These were significant improvements over an established framework (masked KlustaKwik, 18), which needed 480 minutes to sort the 32 channel recording, and 15,000 minutes (10 days) to sort the 128 channel recording, while running on a CPU cluster (we did not attempt to run KlustaKwik on 384 channel recordings).

span.label: The ground-truth spikes are the curated output of one of the two algorithms being compared.
span.quote: To create a hybrid ground truth data set, we first selected all the clusters from a recording that had been previously analyzed with KlustaKwik, and curated by a human expert

span.label: The accuracy benchmark was made by cropping a larger one.
span.quote: We detail here only the 32 channel benchmarks, which we created by cropping the full 128 channel hybrid benchmark (Fig. 3a-c), which we were able to run with many ground truth neurons

span.label: Scores are also reported after a best-possible merging step that no user could perform.
span.quote: Same as (def) after greedy best possible merges. j, Number of merges required to reach best score

span.label: the denoised waveform SUBTRACTED from its original location after being added elsewhere
span.quote: To avoid increasing the spike density at any location on the probe, we also subtracted off the denoised waveform from its original location.

span.label: hybrid ground truth
span.quote: To create a hybrid ground truth data set, we first selected all the clusters from a recording that had been previously analyzed with KlustaKwik, and curated by a human expert

span.quote: To create a hybrid ground truth data set, we first selected all the clusters from a recording that had been previously analyzed with KlustaKwik, and curated by a human expert

span.label: human expert
span.quote: To create a hybrid ground truth data set, we first selected all the clusters from a recording that had been previously analyzed with KlustaKwik, and curated by a human expert

span.label: greedy best possible merges
span.quote: Same as (def) after greedy best possible merges. j, Number of merges required to reach best score

span.label: ground truth neurons
span.quote: We detail here only the 32 channel benchmarks, which we created by cropping the full 128 channel hybrid benchmark (Fig. 3a-c), which we were able to run with many ground truth neurons

span.label: ground truth, here - MANUFACTURED, NOT OBSERVED: the paper's own term is 'hybrid ground truth', and the data set is made by taking human-curated clusters from a previous analysis, denoising their waveforms and re-inserting them elsewhere in a real recording, so the target the sorters must recover is a cleaned copy of an earlier judgement
span.quote: To create a hybrid ground truth data set, we first selected all the clusters from a recording that had been previously analyzed with KlustaKwik, and curated by a human expert

span.label: the reference standard's provenance - THE COMPETITOR'S OUTPUT: the clusters come from a recording previously analysed with KlustaKwik, which is the algorithm Kilosort is being compared against; re-insertion at new locations makes detection a fresh problem, but the standard is still derived from one of the things measured against it
span.quote: To create a hybrid ground truth data set, we first selected all the clusters from a recording that had been previously analyzed with KlustaKwik, and curated by a human expert

span.label: the reported score - GIVEN TWICE, ONCE AFTER AN ORACLE MERGE: the same panels are repeated after greedy best possible merges, with the number of merges needed to reach that best score shown separately, so one of the two numbers is an upper bound rather than an outcome
span.quote: Same as (def) after greedy best possible merges. j, Number of merges required to reach best score

span.label: extends → a previous template-matching method (numbered reference 6)
span.quote: This approach is related to a previous method 6, but that method requires a generic convex optimization that is slow for recordings with large numbers of channels.

span.label: extends → masked KlustaKwik (numbered reference 18)
span.quote: As we demonstrate with constructed ground-truth datasets, our system is more accurate than a current widely-used method 18.

span.label: builds-on → the hybrid ground truth benchmarking technique (numbered reference 18)
span.quote: We compared Kilosort and Klustakwik on 32 and 128 channel recordings, using a technique known as “hybrid ground truth” 18 (Fig. 3a-c).

span.label: hybrid ground truth —operationalised-as→ KlustaKwik
span.quote: To create a hybrid ground truth data set, we first selected all the clusters from a recording that had been previously analyzed with KlustaKwik, and curated by a human expert

span.label: singular value decomposition
span.quote: For each spike, we extracted its raw waveform and denoised it with an SVD decomposition (keeping the top 7 dimensions, so that waveform variability due to bursting and drift could be modeled accurately).

span.label: k-means clustering
span.quote: These N prototypes are then used to initialize a scaled K-means algorithm.

span.label: covariance matrix estimation
span.quote: We then estimate the covariance matrix Σ, and use its singular vectors and singular values E, D to obtain a symmetrical whitening matrix

span.label: Gaussian distribution
span.quote: We modelled this variability with a Gaussian distribution whose variance scales with the square of its mean, to capture the fact that the spikes of neurons closer to the probe vary in relative, not absolute amplitude.

span.label: Kilosort represents the raw voltage as a sum of template waveforms triggered at spike times, which allows spatiotemporally overlapping spikes to be identified and resolved rather than missed.
span.quote: Kilosort models the recorded voltage as a sum of template waveforms triggered on the spike times, allowing overlapping spikes to be identified and resolved.

span.label: Kilosort sorted 32-, 128- and 384-channel recordings in 10, 29 and 140 minutes on one GPU workstation, while KlustaKwik needed 480 minutes for the 32-channel and 15,000 minutes for the 128-channel recording on a CPU cluster.
span.quote: These were significant improvements over an established framework (masked KlustaKwik, 18), which needed 480 minutes to sort the 32 channel recording, and 15,000 minutes (10 days) to sort the 128 channel recording, while running on a CPU cluster

span.label: On hybrid ground-truth data Kilosort yielded well-isolated units (score above 0.9) for 53% of ground-truth neurons versus 35% for KlustaKwik.
span.quote: Both Kilosort and KlustaKwik performed well (Fig. 3d), with Kilosort producing significantly more neurons with well-isolated clusters (53% vs 35% units with scores above 0.9).

span.label: After greedy best-possible operator merges Kilosort still led, 69% of units above score 0.9 against 60% for KlustaKwik.
span.quote: Final best results as well as the required number of matches are shown in Figure 3g-j (Kilosort vs KlustaKwik 69% vs 60% units with scores above 0.9).

span.label: Kilosort's accuracy advantage came from missing fewer spikes rather than from fewer false positives, which the authors attribute to its resolution of overlapping spikes.
span.quote: The relative performance improvement of Kilosort is clearly driven by fewer misses (Fig 3h), which are likely due to its ability to detect overlapping spikes.

span.label: Fitting each spike with its own three-component spatiotemporal SVD ("private PCs") left about five times less residual waveform variance than one common per-channel PCA basis.
span.quote: This approach of tailoring “private PCs” to each spike allows us to fit the spikes with ∼5 times less residual variance than the standard approach of applying a single PCA approximation per channel, to all neurons on that channel

span.label: Kilosort's run time grows linearly with the number of recorded neurons rather than with channel count, so denser electrodes cost no extra processing time.
span.quote: The time taken to run Kilosort scales linearly with the number of recorded neurons, rather than the number of channels, due to the low-dimensional parametrization of template waveforms.

span.label: Kilosort
span.quote: Here we introduce Kilosort, a spike sorting framework that meets these criteria, and show that it allows rapid and accurate sorting of large-scale in vivo data.

span.label: spike sorting
span.quote: When multiple neurons close to the electrode fire action potentials, their spikes must be identified and assigned to the correct neuron based on the features of the recorded waveforms, a process known as spike sorting

span.label: common average referencing
span.quote: To diminish the effect of artifacts shared across all channels, we subtract at each timepoint the median of the signal across all recording sites, an operation known as common average referencing

span.label: zero-phase component analysis (ZCA)
span.quote: use its singular vectors and singular values E, D to obtain a symmetrical whitening matrix that maintains the spatial structure of the data, known as zero-phase component analysis (ZCA)

span.label: hybrid ground truth
span.quote: This technique therefore produces a dataset with very similar spike waveforms, waveform variability, noise, and synchrony to those found in the original data, but where a large set of spike times are known with 100% accuracy.

span.label: private PCs
span.quote: This approach of tailoring “private PCs” to each spike allows us to fit the spikes with ∼5 times less residual variance than the standard approach of applying a single PCA approximation per channel, to all neurons on that channel

span.label: spike-sorting algorithm (Kilosort vs. KlustaKwik)
span.quote: We compared Kilosort and Klustakwik on 32 and 128 channel recordings, using a technique known as “hybrid ground truth”

span.label: number of recording channels (32, 128, 384)
span.quote: The average run times for 32, 128 and 384 channel recordings were 10, 29 and 140 minutes, on a single GPU-equipped workstation (GTX 980Ti).

span.label: processing (run) time
span.quote: To evaluate the algorithm’s performance, we first timed it on several large-scale datasets.

span.label: miss rate and false positive rate (combined into the total score)
span.term: miss rate and false positive rate (combined into the total score)
span.quote: where the false positive rate was normalized by the number of spikes in the test cluster, and the miss rate was normalized by the number of spikes in the ground truth cluster; values close to 1 therefore indicate well-sorted units.

span.label: local spike density on the probe (held constant when building hybrid ground truth)
span.term: local spike density on the probe (held constant when building hybrid ground truth)
span.quote: To avoid increasing the spike density at any location on the probe, we also subtracted off the denoised waveform from its original location.

span.label: 10, 29 and 140 minutes — Kilosort run times for 32-, 128- and 384-channel recordings on a single GTX 980Ti workstation
span.quote: The average run times for 32, 128 and 384 channel recordings were 10, 29 and 140 minutes, on a single GPU-equipped workstation (GTX 980Ti).

span.label: 480 minutes / 15,000 minutes (10 days) — KlustaKwik run times for the 32-channel and 128-channel recordings, the comparison baseline
span.quote: These were significant improvements over an established framework (masked KlustaKwik, 18), which needed 480 minutes to sort the 32 channel recording, and 15,000 minutes (10 days) to sort the 128 channel recording, while running on a CPU cluster

span.label: 53% vs 35% — share of ground-truth neurons sorted with a score above 0.9 by Kilosort versus KlustaKwik before manual merges
span.quote: Both Kilosort and KlustaKwik performed well (Fig. 3d), with Kilosort producing significantly more neurons with well-isolated clusters (53% vs 35% units with scores above 0.9).

span.label: 69% vs 60% — share of units scoring above 0.9 for Kilosort versus KlustaKwik after best possible merges
span.quote: Final best results as well as the required number of matches are shown in Figure 3g-j (Kilosort vs KlustaKwik 69% vs 60% units with scores above 0.9).

span.label: ∼5 times — reduction in residual waveform variance from per-spike private PCs relative to a single per-channel PCA
span.quote: This approach of tailoring “private PCs” to each spike allows us to fit the spikes with ∼5 times less residual variance than the standard approach of applying a single PCA approximation per channel, to all neurons on that channel

span.label: 16 — number of hybrid ground-truth dataset instantiations on which both algorithms were run
span.quote: We ran both Kilosort and KlustaKwik on 16 instantiations of hybrid ground truth data.

span.label: Nchan/Nrank — factor by which the low-rank template decomposition reduces filtering operations, with channel count typically above 100 and template rank typically 3
span.quote: However, the low-rank decomposition of templates allows us to reduce the number of operations by a factor of Nchan/Nrank, where Nchan is the number of channels (typically > 100) and Nrank is the rank of the decomposed template (typically 3).
